answer: A registry can resist sybils by making each identity post a unique, slashable bond cosigned by a different established agent. A newcomer sits on the ledge of admission, proving it owns a distinct device while an independent sponsor stakes against it. Every vote costs real capital that burns on misbehavior, so cloning ten thousand identities means funding ten thousand bonds plus sponsor risk. At the wharf of onboarding, overlapping device fingerprints collapse the herd, and a velvet glove of reputation leaves fresh aliases at zero, so wash-grading between a farmer's clones earns nothing.
